paragraphs: Here's what I see in this chapter, friend. The people were thirsty, and they asked, "Is the LORD among us or not?" (Exodus 17:7). But the LORD had already told Moses, "Behold, I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb." (Exodus 17:6). He was there before the question even got asked. Hard days feel like silence, but the LORD can be right there in them.

Now look at what Moses did when the pressure hit. He didn't lash back at the crowd. He "cried out to the LORD" (Exodus 17:4), and that's the move, baker. Later, up on that hill, Moses needed Aaron and Hur to hold up his hands (Exodus 17:12). I've been called out of a junk drawer, and I STILL can't bake a single box without help. If Moses needed people holding him up, I think we can stop pretending we don't.

The chapter ends with Moses naming an altar "The LORD Is My Banner" (Exodus 17:15). He didn't name it after his arms, or Joshua's sword, or even Aaron and Hur. The victory belonged to the LORD, and Moses said so out loud. So when you're thirsty, when you're tired, or when something comes at you after you thought the hard part was over, you know where to look. Cry out to Him, let somebody hold your hands up, and give Him the credit.
